Phase 50: read-only mode — implementation (round 1). Branch phase-50-read-only-mode, commit 24bbf6f. gate: see entry @ 24bbf6f.

What changed, where:
- tagteam/dualwrite.py: READ_ONLY_ENV / read_only() (one env parse: 0/false/no/empty = off), ReadOnlyError(detail) + DatabaseMissing / SchemaBehind / WalWithoutIndex; writer_lock raises on entry before _ensure_tagteam_dir / lock file / thread lock.
- tagteam/db.py: read_only_connect(project_dir|db_path, require_current_schema=True) — absent → DatabaseMissing (nothing created); -wal without -shm → WalWithoutIndex (fail closed); -wal+-shm → mode=ro; no -wal → mode=ro&immutable=1; PRAGMA query_only=ON; user_version < SCHEMA_VERSION → SchemaBehind, newer tolerated. connect() delegates to it under the switch (all ~70 call sites inherit). @_writes on all 28 INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE functions (source-level test pins the set).
- tagteam/cli.py: main() wraps _dispatch(); ReadOnlyError → message on stderr, exit 2.
- tagteam/headless.py: write_pause/clear_pause/write_cancel/clear_cancel/claim|update|release_turn_slot refuse under the switch (deviation 1 below).
- tagteam/panel.py (lens child) and tagteam/briefer.py (briefer child) set TAGTEAM_READ_ONLY=1 in the child env; headless turns untouched.
- tagteam/hub_api.py: read_only_connect delegates to db.read_only_connect(require_current_schema=False) — fixes plain mode=ro failing on a sidecar-less WAL DB; None-on-absent / ProjectDataError-on-corrupt kept.
- tagteam/usage.py, briefer.brief_command, controls.interject --list: DatabaseMissing → empty result.
- Contract: 'Read-only helpers' paragraph before 'Mid-review amendment', identical in all three copies; vendored_contract_hashes.json regenerated (contract_hashes.py --check passes).
- tests/test_readonly.py (41 tests): switch parse; writer_lock creates nothing; read_only_connect one test per sidecar row incl. crash-copy WAL fixtures (wal_autocheckpoint=0 under an open writer) — WAL+SHM sees the WAL-held row with .db/-wal unchanged and only -shm allowed to differ, WAL-only refused with no -shm created, SHM-only/neither identical; old schema refused and un-migrated, newer readable; query_only; every-writer-decorated; runtime markers; CLI write commands (cycle add/init, state set, interject, pause, rule on an escalated cycle) → exit 2 + tree identical; read commands → work; the six-state snapshot matrix (fresh / neither / wal+shm / wal-only / shm-only / old-schema × 12 read commands, every path+bytes under the project); panel lens child sees the switch, briefer child sees it, headless turn child does not (and its round still lands); hub sidecar-less open. tests/fixtures/fake_agent.py records the switch it saw and, for rogue lenses, the write attempt. tests/test_panel.py: rogue lens now refused (exit 2, no round, panel falls back — new test); post-hoc detection kept via a 'rogue-unset' lens that clears the switch.

Deviations from the approved plan (all in the phase doc, 'Implementation notes'): (1) pause/cancel/turn-slot markers were NOT under writer_lock as the plan assumed — they got their own guard; (2) brief on an absent DB keeps the command's existing empty semantics (text exit 1 / --json exit 0) instead of a blanket exit 0; (3) cycle rounds reads canonical files, so the CLI-level WAL-visibility assertion uses usage --json; (4) hub opts out of the schema check (reads v3–v5 by design, existing test); (5) child-env and hub tests live in test_readonly.py rather than spread across files.

Measured before/while implementing (SQLite 3.51): plain mode=ro cannot open a sidecar-less WAL DB; immutable=1 ignores WAL frames; WAL-only under mode=ro creates -shm — the rule follows those facts. Focused runs: test_readonly + test_hub_api/plugin/dualwrite/db/controls/briefer/panel/headless/cycle all green before submit.

Round 2 — gate bounce r1 addressed: tests/test_docs_story.py locates the CLI dispatch table by slicing cli.py from 'def main('; the Phase 50 wrapper had moved the table into _dispatch() defined above it. main() now precedes _dispatch() (order only, no behaviour change), commit c1a4969. Everything else as in round 1 (24bbf6f). gate: see entry @ c1a4969.

GATE: PASS | scope 16 paths | plan-doc ok | tests ok (1601 passed, 5 skipped, 4m54s)
checked: HEAD c1a4969

Three write bypasses remain outside the new guards.

1. `tagteam migrate --force` can delete the project database under `TAGTEAM_READ_ONLY=1`. In `_migrate_runtime_db_command`, an existing populated DB is opened read-only, its counts are read, and then `_remove_sqlite_db_files(db_path)` runs before the later guarded `db.connect`/`db.import_from_files` call. The command therefore removes `.db`, `-wal`, and `-shm` and only then fails with `DatabaseMissing`. Guard the destructive helper/path before any unlink (while preserving `migrate --dry-run` as a read operation), and add a CLI regression test over a populated DB asserting exit 2 and a byte/path-identical tree.

2. `tagteam state repair-db --force-clear` calls `dualwrite.clear_db_invalid()` without `writer_lock` or another read-only check, so a helper can delete `.tagteam/DB_INVALID`. Put the refusal at the low-level sentinel mutator (and cover `mark_db_invalid` as appropriate), or guard the command before deletion. Add a CLI test with a real sentinel asserting exit 2 and unchanged bytes.

3. `tagteam cancel-turn` has a stale-metadata cleanup path that directly calls `h.inflight_path(root).unlink()` in `controls.py`, bypassing `write_cancel`/`clear_cancel` and `_refuse_if_read_only()`. A read-only helper presented with stale inflight metadata can remove the marker. Guard this cleanup or the mutating command before the unlink, and test the stale-inflight case for exit 2 and an unchanged marker/tree. The valid-inflight path is already stopped by guarded `write_cancel` before process signalling, but should also be pinned if practical.

Please expand the CLI write matrix to the remaining approved/documented mutators (`resume`, `gate run`, and relevant `state reset|diagnose --clean|sync|repair-db` paths), not only the current `cycle add/init`, `state set`, `interject`, `pause`, and separate `rule` test. This both closes the three concrete holes and makes the “every cycle-writing command” claim resistant to another direct filesystem path.

Gatekeeper passed at HEAD c1a4969 (1601 passed, 5 skipped); I did not rerun the full suite. Apart from these bypasses, the connection semantics, decorators, CLI error boundary, child environments, contract copies, sidecar matrix, and gate-bounce correction look sound.
